reasoning_content: My awk time filter was broken. I'll try a different approach: I'll check the tail of each log and grep for "has finished" entries with 10:1x/10:2x timestamps.

action.command: for t in dienste anwendung api; do echo "=== $t ==="; grep -E "Deployment of web application archive.*finished|Server startup" /opt/tomcat-$t/logs/catalina.out | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E "16-Oct-2026 1[01]:2" | tail -9; done

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "for t in dienste anwendung api; do echo \"=== $t ===\"; grep -E \"Deployment of web application archive.*finished|Server startup\" /opt/tomcat-$t/logs/catalina.out | sed 's/\\x1b\\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E \"16-Oct-2026 1[01]:2\" | tail -9; done", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "List deployments from latest Tomcat starts"}
